newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamist PM visits president for talks.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamist PM visits president for talks.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan met President Suleyman Demirel on Thursday for regular talks against a background of rising tensions between the Islamist-led government and the secular establishment.
Erbakan arrived at the presidential palace shortly after 5.00 p.m. (1500 GMT).
The president's press office earlier denied media reports that Demirel had sent Erbakan a letter expressing concern the government was at odds with the secular system.
Erbakan described the press reports as "a lie".
"There is a widespread feeling that you are diverting from the secularist, democratic republican aims. This is also my belief," the mass-selling Hurriyet daily quoted Demirel as saying in the letter.

The newspapers said the alleged letter was also copied to armed forces leader Ismail Hakki Karadayi ahead of Friday's crucial meeting between top politicians and the restive chiefs of the secularist armed forces.

The armed forces have warned Erbakan's Islamist-right coalition in recent weeks against increasing the role of Islam in public life, and these issues are expected to be discussed at Friday's meeting of the National Security Council.
Demirel, himself dislodged as premier during two of the three previous coups, allegedly warned Erbakan against the consequences of upsetting the army and other groups.
